issues.issue: Whether the bank became liable to pay the tax debtor (Mr. McLeod) upon receiving cheques payable to him for deposit into a joint account under s. 224(1) ITA.
issues.applicant_position: Trustco argues it was not liable to pay McLeod personally as cheques were deposited to joint account; liability arises only on proper presentment as drawee.
issues.respondent_position: Canada contends bank became liable on cheque acceptance for deposit; no distinction between presentment for cash or deposit; McLeod's depositor role irrelevant.
issues.result_text: Bank's liability triggered only on presentment for payment; deposit to joint account does not make bank liable to pay McLeod personally.

issues.issue: Whether funds in the joint account are payable to both account holders or only to the payee (Mr. McLeod) for purposes of s. 224(1) ITA.
issues.respondent_position: Deschamps J. argues funds in joint account are payable to both holders; dissenting judge says funds are payable only to payee while in transit.
issues.result_text: Funds in joint account are joint property; before deposit, bank liable only to payee; other joint holder has no right to funds in transit.
